boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain College of Charleston
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night food stops for College of Charleston students, focusing on under-21-safe spots near campus that stay open for post-study or weekend cravings.

cards.title: Benny Ravello's
cards.subtitle: Giant Slices on Upper King
cards.notes: Grab a massive 28-inch pizza slice at this Upper King staple. It is a go-to for students needing a quick, affordable late-night bite before heading back to the dorms.
cards.short_summary: A popular pizza shop on King Street known for its oversized slices and late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: Benny Ravello's is open until 1:00 AM Sunday through Wednesday and until 2:00 AM Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Benny Ravello's
cards.access_notes: Open until 2 AM on weekends; counter service is fast and under-21 friendly.

cards.title: Gilroy's Pizza Pub
cards.subtitle: Late-Night King Street Classic
cards.notes: Visit Charleston's oldest pizza joint for greasy, reliable slices. It has served the college crowd for decades and stays open later than almost anywhere else downtown.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing pizza pub on King Street famous for its very late operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Gilroy's Pizza Pub is open until 3:00 AM Sunday through Thursday and until 4:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late-Night Eats: Charleston - South Carolina Tourism
cards.access_notes: Open until 4 AM on weekends; strictly a food-focused run for students after hours.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Warm Cookies on King Street
cards.notes: Stop by for warm, fresh-baked cookies or ice cream sandwiches. This spot is a favorite for late-night study breaks and sweet cravings near the campus core.
cards.short_summary: A bakery chain specializing in late-night cookie delivery and walk-up service.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies at 509 King St offers late-night hours, typically serving until 1:00 AM or later.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies | 509 King St Charleston
cards.access_notes: Open late for walk-ins and delivery; perfect for dorm-room snacking.

cards.title: City Bistro
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Late-Night Dining
cards.notes: Head to Berry Hall for an all-you-care-to-eat late-night snack. It is the primary on-campus option for students using meal taps after standard dining hours.
cards.short_summary: The College of Charleston's bistro-style dining hall located in Berry Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus dining locations like City Bistro serve students until 10:00 PM daily and until midnight on weekends.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Accepts Meal Taps and Cougar Cash; open until midnight on Friday and Saturday.

cards.title: The Market at Berry Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Convenience Store
cards.notes: Pick up microwavable meals, fresh fruit, or grab-and-go snacks. This on-campus market is the reliable stop for dorm essentials and late-night fuel.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus convenience store providing snacks and meals for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Market carries late-night snacks and microwavable meals and is listed as a key campus dining location.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Located in Berry Hall; accepts Cougar Cash and Dining Dollars.

cards.title: Kaminsky's Dessert Cafe
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Sweets at the Market
cards.notes: Enjoy a slice of rotating cake or a signature milkshake in a cozy setting. It is a popular spot for students to wind down with dessert after a night out.
cards.short_summary: A well-known dessert cafe in the French Quarter offering a wide variety of treats.
cards.evidence_claim: Kaminsky's is open until 11:00 PM Sunday through Thursday and until 1:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Kaminsky's Dessert Café Charleston
cards.access_notes: Under-21 safe; often has a line on weekends due to its popularity for late-night treats.

cards.title: Waffle House
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Breakfast Run
cards.notes: Visit this classic 24-hour diner for hashbrowns and waffles. While a short drive or ride from campus, it remains a quintessential late-night destination for students.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour breakfast chain restaurant located near the downtown area.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House locations in Charleston are generally open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.source_title: Waffle House #411 Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; always available for late-night dining regardless of the day.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Drive-Thru
cards.notes: Stop by the Spring Street location for a quick late-night meal. It is one of the few fast-food options near campus with extended hours on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A fast-food restaurant on Spring Street offering late-night and 24-hour service.
cards.evidence_claim: The McDonald's at 230 Spring St is open 24 hours on Friday and Saturday, and until midnight on other days.
cards.source_title: McDonald's 230 Spring St, Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru and lobby hours vary; 24-hour service available on weekends.

cards.title: Callie's Hot Little Biscuit
cards.subtitle: Weekend Late-Night Biscuits
cards.notes: Grab a savory or sweet biscuit at this Upper King window. It is a unique Charleston tradition that opens specifically for the late-night weekend crowd.
cards.short_summary: A famous biscuit shop that offers late-night service on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Callie's Hot Little Biscuit on King St offers late-night service from 10:00 PM to 2:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.source_title: Guilty Pleasure: Callie's Hot Little Biscuit
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours are exclusive to Friday and Saturday nights; walk-up window service.

cards.title: The Rarebit
cards.subtitle: Retro Diner Comfort Food
cards.notes: Enjoy breakfast for dinner or a patty melt in this vintage-style diner. It is a more sit-down late-night option for students looking for comfort food on King Street.
cards.short_summary: A retro-themed diner on Upper King Street known for its late-night comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rarebit is open until 1:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays, serving a full menu of comfort classics.
cards.source_title: The Rarebit Charleston
cards.access_notes: Under-21 safe for dining; kitchen serves the full menu until closing on weekends.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student spaces and quiet corners of the College of Charleston that go beyond the standard historic highlights.

cards.title: Rivers Green
cards.subtitle: Outdoor study lawn behind Addlestone Library
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or snag a hammock for outdoor studying. It is a popular spot for sunbathing between classes with easy access to the library's Starbucks.
cards.short_summary: A large grassy area behind the main library used for outdoor studying and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Green is described as a natural study spot where students bring textbooks to enjoy the sun, often using hammocks or patio furniture.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Students' Top 5 Study Spots in the Sun
cards.access_notes: Open public campus green space; best during daylight hours.

cards.title: Addlestone Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Designated silent study zone
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for absolute silence. Room 311 is specifically designated for silent study without a reservation for those needing deep focus.
cards.short_summary: The quietest floor of the main library, featuring silent study rooms and special collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor is designated for quiet study, with room 311 available for silent study without a reservation.
cards.source_title: Studying in Addlestone - College of Charleston Libraries
cards.access_notes: Requires Cougar Card for late-night access; visitors allowed 9am-5pm with ID.

cards.entity_name: Rita Liddy Hollings Science Center Roof Deck
cards.title: Hollings Science Center Roof Deck
cards.subtitle: Rooftop telescope and viewing area
cards.notes: Visit the fourth-floor roof for astronomy nights. It features telescope mounts and a viewing deck used by biology, physics, and astronomy students.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop facility at the science center used for astronomy labs and community viewing events.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth-floor roof houses an astronomy lab, telescope dome, and a publicly accessible roof deck for 'Astronomy Nights'.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Rita Hollings Science Center - HDR
cards.access_notes: Access typically during scheduled astronomy events or for science students.

cards.title: Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Contemporary art gallery in the Marion and Wayland H. Cato Jr. Center
cards.notes: Explore rotating contemporary exhibitions for free. The gallery is open until 7pm on Thursdays, making it a great late-afternoon cultural stop.
cards.short_summary: A non-collecting contemporary art museum on campus that hosts adventurous exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Halsey Institute is free and open to the public, with hours extending to 7pm on Thursdays during exhibitions.
cards.source_title: VISIT - Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday 11am-4pm; Thursdays until 7pm.

cards.title: Stern Student Center Game Room
cards.subtitle: Student recreation and gaming hub
cards.notes: Located on the second floor, this space features video games and pool tables. It's a central spot for taking a break between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated recreation area for students featuring gaming consoles and billiards.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stern Student Center includes a game room with video games and pool tables as part of its student life facilities.
cards.source_title: Naming Opportunities - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Building undergoing renovations through late 2026; check current access for specific rooms.

cards.entity_name: School of Science and Mathematics Atrium
cards.title: SSMB Atrium
cards.subtitle: Study space with natural history displays
cards.notes: Study under pterodactyl skeletons and beside a fish tank. This quiet atrium offers tables and whiteboards on multiple floors for student use.
cards.short_summary: A bright, multi-story atrium in the science building used for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Science and Mathematics building features a beautiful atrium with skeletons and fish tanks, plus study corners with whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Hitting the Books: Secret Study Spots
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; generally quieter than the library.

cards.title: Cougar Mall Fountain
cards.subtitle: Central campus meeting spot
cards.notes: Known by alumni as 'The Spot,' this fountain is a major intersection for meeting friends or professors between classes in Maybank Hall.
cards.short_summary: A central fountain and plaza area that serves as a primary social hub on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The fountain in Cougar Mall is described as a favorite meeting location for students and professors between classes.
cards.source_title: My Space: The Cougar Mall Fountain
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plaza; non-amplified sound space.

cards.title: Avery Research Center
cards.subtitle: African American history and culture center
cards.notes: Visit for self-guided museum tours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. It preserves the unique history of the African diaspora in the Lowcountry.
cards.short_summary: A research center and museum dedicated to African American history and culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Avery Research Center offers self-guided tours and houses archives available by appointment.
cards.source_title: Visit - Avery Research Center
cards.access_notes: Museum tours Mon/Wed/Fri; Reading room by appointment only.

cards.title: Education Center 24/7 Space
cards.subtitle: Round-the-clock study location
cards.notes: A reliable 24/7 study spot for students when the library is closed. It is a favorite for late-night sessions and marathon studying.
cards.short_summary: An academic building known among students for providing 24-hour study access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Education Center is noted as a 24/7 study location for students.
cards.source_title: Favorite Study Locations at CofC – The Honor Roll
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 for students with valid ID.

cards.title: Cistern Yard
cards.subtitle: Historic green with live oaks
cards.notes: While iconic for graduation, students use this daily for 'cisternating'—socializing or studying under the Spanish moss-draped live oaks.
cards.short_summary: The historic heart of campus, used for both major ceremonies and daily student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Cistern Yard serves as a gathering place for students to socialize and study, a practice historically called 'cisternating'.
cards.source_title: The CofC Cistern: More Than Meets the Eye
cards.access_notes: Open public campus space; often used for events.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and cultural activities at the College of Charleston, from historic campus courtyards to modern art galleries and scenic city parks.

cards.title: Relax Under the Oaks at Cistern Yard
cards.subtitle: Historic heart of campus
cards.notes: Find a spot on the grass or a bench under the massive live oaks. This iconic green space is open to the public and serves as the college's primary social hub.
cards.short_summary: A historic, oak-shaded courtyard at the center of campus used for relaxing and major events.
cards.evidence_claim: Cistern Yard is the heart of the College of Charleston campus, serving as a green space for generations of students. It is generally accessible to the public.
cards.source_title: Cistern Yard: Campus green, graduation venue and performance space
cards.access_notes: Open daily to the public; some areas may be restricted during private events or commencement.

cards.title: Explore Modern Art at the Halsey
cards.subtitle: Free contemporary art museum
cards.notes: Walk through rotating exhibitions of adventurous contemporary art. Admission is always free for students and the general public during gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: A non-collecting contemporary art museum on campus offering free admission to all visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art is completely free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: VISIT - Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM, with extended hours until 7:00 PM on Thursdays.

cards.entity_name: Mace Brown Museum of Natural History
cards.title: See Fossils at the Mace Brown Museum
cards.subtitle: On-campus paleontology museum
cards.notes: View over 3,000 fossils, including a 40-foot shark jaw and dinosaur skeletons. It is located on the second floor of the School of Science and Mathematics Building.
cards.short_summary: A free natural history museum featuring a vast collection of fossils and marine life specimens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mace Brown Museum of Natural History is open to the public and admission is free.
cards.source_title: Mace Brown Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Open daily 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM; closed on Wednesdays.

cards.title: Study Outdoors at Rivers Green
cards.subtitle: Plaza behind Addlestone Library
cards.notes: Utilize the outdoor tables, chairs, and fountains for a scenic study session. This space offers free campus Wi-Fi and is a popular student gathering spot.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped plaza behind the main library featuring seating, fountains, and outdoor Wi-Fi.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Green features water fountains, benches, and a patio with tables and chairs for student use.
cards.source_title: Addlestone Library & Rivers Green
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; student tabling allowed with reservations.

cards.title: Visit the Avery Research Center
cards.subtitle: African American history and culture
cards.notes: Take a self-guided tour of the museum galleries to learn about the history of the African diaspora in the Lowcountry. Advance registration is requested.
cards.short_summary: A research center and museum dedicated to African American history with free public tours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Avery Research Center invites the general public to access the center's archives on a self-guided tour; admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit - Avery Research Center
cards.access_notes: Self-guided tours available Mon, Wed, Fri 10:30 AM - 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM - 3:30 PM.

cards.title: Walk to the Pineapple Fountain
cards.subtitle: Scenic harbor views
cards.notes: Walk ten minutes from campus to this award-winning park. Sit on the pier swings or wade in the iconic Pineapple Fountain for free.
cards.short_summary: A prominent city park along the Cooper River featuring the famous Pineapple Fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Enjoy the beauty of Waterfront Park for free; there is no admission fee. It is a 10-minute walk from Cougar Mall.
cards.source_title: How to Get Around Charleston as a CofC Student
cards.access_notes: Open daily to the public from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Stroll Around Colonial Lake
cards.subtitle: Historic tidal pond and park
cards.notes: Enjoy a walk or jog around the wide perimeter path of this historic park. It features plenty of benches and free public Wi-Fi provided by the city.
cards.short_summary: A popular city park centered around a large tidal pond, ideal for walking and relaxing.
cards.evidence_claim: Colonial Lake is a cherished recreational area with broad walkways and free internet access for the public.
cards.source_title: Free internet access at public parks in Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily; free Wi-Fi available on-site.

cards.title: People Watch at Cougar Mall
cards.subtitle: Central campus thoroughfare
cards.notes: Grab a seat on a bench in this pedestrian-only zone. It's the best spot on campus to see student life in action or find free student-led events.
cards.short_summary: The main pedestrian walkway on campus, serving as a hub for student activity and tabling.
cards.evidence_claim: Cougar Mall is a non-amplified sound space used for student organization tabling and campus life.
cards.source_title: Facility Features - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public pedestrian thoroughfare.

cards.title: Browse the Stacks at Addlestone
cards.subtitle: Main campus library
cards.notes: Visitors can access the library for free during daytime hours. Use the first floor for quiet conversation or head to the upper floors for silent study.
cards.short_summary: The university's primary library, offering free daytime access to the public and students.
cards.evidence_claim: Visitors may access Addlestone Library Monday-Friday, 9 am-5 pm, with a government-issued ID.
cards.source_title: Access the Libraries - College of Charleston Libraries
cards.access_notes: Public access Mon-Fri 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Cougar Card required for after-hours student access.

cards.title: Play Games at the Stern Center
cards.subtitle: Student social and gaming hub
cards.notes: Join the Table-Top Gaming Club for free weekly sessions featuring board games and JackBox. Most student-led events here are free for the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A student center hosting free gaming events and social activities for the college community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Table-Top Gaming Club meets weekly at the Stern Student Center for free gaming sessions open to students.
cards.source_title: Table-Top Gaming Club Free-for-All!
cards.access_notes: Events typically held in Room 201 or 206; check Cougar Connect for current schedules.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the silent upper floors of Addlestone to the sun-drenched alcoves of the Rita Hollings Science Center, these ten spots offer the best environments for focused work on campus.

cards.title: Third Floor Silent Zone
cards.subtitle: Addlestone Library
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for strictly silent study; even earbuds must be kept at low volume to maintain the quiet atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent study floor of the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2nd and 3rd floors of Addlestone Library are reserved for silent study and listening only through earbuds.
cards.source_title: Q. Where can I study in Addlestone Library? - Ask Us!
cards.access_notes: Open to students with Cougar Card; check library site for seasonal hours.

cards.title: Science Center Window Alcoves
cards.subtitle: Rita Hollings Science Center
cards.notes: Utilize the built-in whiteboards and natural light in the hallway alcoves for collaborative STEM problem-solving sessions.
cards.short_summary: Modern study alcoves with whiteboards and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rita Liddy Hollings Science Center features dynamic seating options, ample windows, and whiteboards on every floor.
cards.source_title: Lovely Rita Liddy Hollings Science Center - The College Today
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during academic building hours.

cards.title: Rivers Green Tables
cards.subtitle: Behind Addlestone Library
cards.notes: Grab a patio table behind the library for an outdoor session with easy access to the nearby Starbucks for caffeine breaks.
cards.short_summary: A popular outdoor green space with tables and Wi-Fi connectivity.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Green is a preferred outdoor study spot with plenty of tables and patio furniture located behind the library.
cards.source_title: Favorite Study Locations at CofC – The Honor Roll
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; well-lit at night with campus security nearby.

cards.title: Stern Center Upper Lounges
cards.subtitle: Stern Student Center
cards.notes: Visit the second, third, or fourth floors for quieter lounge seating away from the high-traffic first-floor game room.
cards.short_summary: Multi-level student center offering various lounge and table setups.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stern Center has computers on the first floor and study spaces on the second, third, and fourth floors.
cards.source_title: Stern Student Center - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Requires Cougar Card for entry after hours; check for finals week extensions.

cards.title: Beatty Center Atrium
cards.subtitle: School of Business
cards.notes: Study in the light-filled atrium of the business school, which offers a professional atmosphere and ample seating.
cards.short_summary: A high-ceilinged atrium in the School of Business with natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beatty Center Atrium is cited as a fan-favorite study location for business majors and others.
cards.source_title: School of Business Facilities - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic building hours.

cards.title: Education Center 24/7 Lounge
cards.subtitle: Education Center
cards.notes: Access this building 24/7 for late-night sessions; it is a reliable alternative when the library closes.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour accessible academic building with dedicated study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Education Center is noted for being open 24/7 for student study needs.
cards.source_title: Favorite Study Locations at CofC – The Honor Roll
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access typically requires a valid Cougar Card for entry.

cards.title: Harbor Walk Waterfront Seating
cards.subtitle: Computer Science Department
cards.notes: Enjoy views of the Cooper River and Ravenel Bridge while studying on the outdoor balconies of this waterfront complex.
cards.short_summary: Waterfront study areas located at the Aquarium Wharf campus extension.
cards.evidence_claim: Harbor Walk features a balcony overlooking the Cooper River and provides a quiet place for schoolwork.
cards.source_title: My Space: Harbor Walk, Room 319 - The College Today
cards.access_notes: Located about a mile from main campus; accessible via CARTA bus or bike.

cards.title: Hillel Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Jewish Studies Center
cards.notes: Relax in the comfy study areas of the Hillel Lounge; don't miss Bagel Tuesday for a mid-study snack.
cards.short_summary: A cozy student lounge with a home-like atmosphere for focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jewish Studies Center houses comfy study areas and the Hillel Student Lounge for student use.
cards.source_title: Our Building | Charleston Hillel
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; check for specific Hillel event schedules.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Addlestone Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room online for groups of 3+; these spaces include whiteboards and are ideal for group projects.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms equipped with whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Collaborative Study Rooms may be reserved for groups of 3 or more persons for up to two hours per day.
cards.source_title: Q. Where can I study in Addlestone Library? - Ask Us!
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via LibCal; Cougar Card needed for check-in.

cards.title: Phillis Wheatley Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Avery Research Center
cards.notes: Book an appointment for a highly focused, scholarly environment surrounded by African American history and culture.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, appointment-only reading room for specialized research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Phillis Wheatley Literary and Social Club Reading Room is open by appointment for on-site research.
cards.source_title: Using Collections - Avery Research Center
cards.access_notes: Appointment required at least two business days in advance.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the historic streets and vibrant corridors surrounding the College of Charleston, where campus life blends seamlessly into the Holy City's downtown.

cards.title: The Main Retail Artery
cards.subtitle: King Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this historic corridor for major retail brands and local boutiques. It serves as the primary social and shopping spine for students just steps from campus.
cards.short_summary: King Street is Charleston's premier shopping and dining destination, bordering the eastern edge of the college campus.
cards.evidence_claim: King Street serves as the main artery for foot and auto traffic, leading to staple spots for food and shopping near the university.
cards.source_title: An Insider's Guide to Upper King Street - The Local Palate
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; most shops open daily from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The Academic Gateway
cards.subtitle: George Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the School of Business or grab a coffee at Caviar & Bananas. This street connects the heart of campus to the King Street shopping district.
cards.short_summary: George Street is a central campus thoroughfare housing the School of Business and popular student cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Business is located at 66 George Street, and local cafes like Caviar & Bananas are popular student options on this street.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Students' Top 5 Study Spots in the Sun
cards.access_notes: Public street; university buildings typically open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM for visitors.

cards.title: The Residential Hub
cards.subtitle: St. Philip Street Corridor
cards.notes: Navigate this north-south route to find major residence halls like Berry and McAlister, plus the popular Greek eatery Stella's.
cards.short_summary: St. Philip Street is a primary residential corridor for students, featuring several large dormitories and local dining.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Philip Street is home to Berry and McAlister residence halls and the restaurant Stella's, owned by CofC alumni.
cards.source_title: Find 9 Great Restaurants Right Next to the College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public street; residence halls require student ID for entry.

cards.title: The Civic Boundary
cards.subtitle: Calhoun Street Corridor
cards.notes: Cross this busy street to reach Marion Square or the Addlestone Library. It serves as the northern boundary of the historic campus core.
cards.short_summary: Calhoun Street is a major east-west thoroughfare that separates the main campus from the medical district and Marion Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Calhoun Street is a major boundary for the campus, with the Addlestone Library and Marion Square located nearby.
cards.source_title: A History of the College's Land: Locating the Land
cards.access_notes: Major public thoroughfare; open 24/7.

cards.title: Historic House Row
cards.subtitle: Wentworth Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past preserved historic homes used as student housing. Stop by The Rise for coffee or head west toward Colonial Lake.
cards.short_summary: Wentworth Street features historic university-owned houses and popular local coffee shops like The Rise.
cards.evidence_claim: Wentworth Street contains historic houses for upperclass students and the popular study spot The Rise coffee shop.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Students' Top 5 Study Spots in the Sun
cards.access_notes: Public street; historic houses are private residences for students.

cards.title: The Library Link
cards.subtitle: Coming Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find the Addlestone Library and the future site of Coming Street Commons. This street is a key path for students moving between classes.
cards.short_summary: Coming Street runs through the western side of campus, providing access to the main library and student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Coming Street is the location of the Addlestone Library and the proposed Coming Street Commons student housing project.
cards.source_title: Coming Street Commons - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public street; library hours vary by semester.

cards.title: The President's Path
cards.subtitle: Glebe Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll this quiet, narrow street to see the Bishop Robert Smith House (the President's House) and several historic student residences.
cards.short_summary: Glebe Street is a historic, picturesque lane housing the university president and several student residences.
cards.evidence_claim: Glebe Street is home to the President's House and historic houses for students just steps from the Cistern Yard.
cards.source_title: The President's House: Bishop Robert Smith House
cards.access_notes: Public street; the President's House is a private residence.

cards.title: The Dining Destination
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here for the Liberty Street Fresh Food Company, the campus's main all-you-care-to-eat dining hall, located below Liberty Hall.
cards.short_summary: Liberty Street is a short but vital campus corridor housing a major dining hall and freshman residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Liberty Street Residence Hall is located above the Liberty Street Fresh Food Company dining location.
cards.source_title: Liberty Hall - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public street; dining hall access requires a meal plan or payment.

cards.title: The Southern Edge
cards.subtitle: Beaufain Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the southern boundary of the campus area, where you'll find local favorites like Second State Coffee for a quiet study session.
cards.short_summary: Beaufain Street marks the southern transition from the college campus into the Harleston Village neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: Second State Coffee on Beaufain Street is a popular spot for students to decompress or work.
cards.source_title: Things to Do Near Wentworth Mansion | Charleston Guide
cards.access_notes: Public street; coffee shop hours typically 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The Ansonborough Link
cards.subtitle: Society Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk east toward the Ansonborough neighborhood to find quiet residential blocks and historic architecture popular with upperclassmen.
cards.short_summary: Society Street connects the college area to the historic Ansonborough district, known for its well-preserved 19th-century homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Society Street is located in the Ansonborough neighborhood, featuring historic character and proximity to downtown dining.
cards.source_title: 29 Society St Charleston SC | Zillow
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; open 24/7.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and storied customs of the College of Charleston, from white-clad graduations in the Cistern Yard to the superstitions of Porter's Lodge.

cards.title: White Dresses and Dinner Jackets
cards.subtitle: A formal alternative to caps and gowns
cards.notes: Skip the polyester robes; spring graduates wear white dresses or white dinner jackets with a red rose or boutonniere, a tradition dating back to the early 20th century.
cards.short_summary: CofC spring graduates wear formal white attire instead of traditional academic regalia.
cards.evidence_claim: At the College of Charleston, spring graduates completing their undergraduate degrees do not don robes or caps — instead, they wear white dresses or white dinner jackets.
cards.source_title: Traditions - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Visible during the annual spring commencement ceremony in May.

cards.title: The 'Know Thyself' Passage
cards.subtitle: Entering and exiting the Cistern Yard
cards.notes: Walk through the archway on your first day for Convocation and exit through it after Graduation to symbolize your journey into the world.
cards.short_summary: Students pass through the Porter's Lodge archway at the start and end of their college careers.
cards.evidence_claim: Students at the College of Charleston pass through the arch at Porter's Lodge on their first day... Upon graduation in the spring, students exit the Cistern Yard by passing underneath the same arch.
cards.source_title: Traditions - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: The archway is located on George Street and is accessible to the public.

cards.title: Don't Cross the Cistern
cards.subtitle: A jinx on your graduation date
cards.notes: Avoid walking across the raised grassy oval of the Cistern before you graduate, or legend says you won't finish your degree on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition warns students not to walk across the Cistern until they graduate.
cards.evidence_claim: In the 21st century, however, some students believe that walking across the Cistern before finishing their education will jinx their chances of graduating.
cards.source_title: Get Ready For Graduation: Four Facts About the Cistern
cards.access_notes: The Cistern Yard is a central campus green open to students and visitors.

cards.title: Turning the Ring
cards.subtitle: A signet-style rite of passage
cards.notes: Wear your school ring with the seal upside down until commencement, then turn it right-side up to signify your status as an alumnus.
cards.short_summary: Graduates turn their school rings right-side up during the commencement ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: At Commencement, College of Charleston students are called upon to 'turn the ring'... so the seal is facing right side up as they go out into the world.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Ring Tradition
cards.access_notes: The ring ceremony and turning of the ring occur annually for eligible students.

cards.title: Pep Supper
cards.subtitle: A century of spirit and service
cards.notes: Attend this high-energy dance competition and food drive that kicks off basketball season, a tradition that has evolved over nearly 100 years.
cards.short_summary: Pep Supper is a long-standing tradition featuring a dance contest and food drive for the Lowcountry Food Bank.
cards.evidence_claim: Pep Supper is one of the oldest traditions at the College, dating back almost 100 years... transformed the celebration into a weeklong fundraiser and food drive.
cards.source_title: CofC Alumni Pep Supper Supports Fraternity, Sorority Life
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall, typically at the TD Arena.

cards.title: Signing the Book
cards.subtitle: Official entry into the academic community
cards.notes: Join your classmates during Convocation to officially sign the College's ledger, marking your formal induction into the student body.
cards.short_summary: New students sign a formal ledger during Convocation to mark their entry into the College.
cards.evidence_claim: Students at the College of Charleston pass through the arch at Porter's Lodge on their first day and enter the Cistern Yard to officially sign 'the book.'
cards.source_title: Traditions - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the annual Convocation ceremony in August.

cards.title: The Ghosts of Berry Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus legends of the old orphanage
cards.notes: Listen for the sounds of phantom marbles or children's voices in this residence hall, built on the site of a former orphanage.
cards.short_summary: Berry Residence Hall is the subject of long-standing campus ghost stories related to its history as an orphanage site.
cards.evidence_claim: Students then reported hearing distant voices and laughter of children late into the night. Some students also said that they were awakened by the sound of marbles cascading across the floor.
cards.source_title: 3 Tales of College of Charleston Ghosts
cards.access_notes: Residence hall access is restricted to students, but the exterior is visible on St. Philip Street.

cards.title: Maroon Mayhem
cards.subtitle: The ultimate back-to-school bash
cards.notes: Celebrate the start of the year with this street festival featuring games, food, and music right in the heart of campus.
cards.short_summary: Maroon Mayhem is an annual street festival held during the first week of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: A good time was had by all at the 2023 Maroon Mayhem, the College's annual street festival celebrating the return of students to campus.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Photos of the Week
cards.access_notes: Held annually in August during the 'Weeks of Welcome.'

cards.entity_name: Ring Night at the President's House
cards.title: Instilling History in the Rings
cards.subtitle: A night at 6 Glebe Street
cards.notes: Before the ring ceremony, all student rings spend the night in the President's House to be 'instilled' with the College's 250-year history.
cards.short_summary: Student rings are housed in the historic President's House the night before they are presented.
cards.evidence_claim: Tradition dictates that the night before each Ring Ceremony, the rings spend the night in the College's original classroom in the President's House at 6 Glebe Street.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Ring Tradition
cards.access_notes: The President's House is a private residence, but the tradition is part of the official ring program.

cards.title: Rubbing the Cougar Paw
cards.subtitle: Luck from the campus mascot
cards.notes: Visit the Clyde the Cougar statues on campus for a photo op or a quick rub of the paw for good luck before a big game or exam.
cards.short_summary: Two statues of the mascot Clyde the Cougar serve as campus landmarks and symbols of school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Clyde the Cougar is beloved by young and old and is represented in two statues on campus.
cards.source_title: Traditions from the CofC Traditions App
cards.access_notes: Statues are located in Cougar Mall and near the TD Arena.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at College of Charleston, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Step Through the Arch
cards.subtitle: The Official Welcome Tradition
cards.notes: Walk through the archway inscribed with 'Know Thyself' to enter the Cistern Yard. This symbolic entry marks your official start as a member of the College community.
cards.short_summary: A historic archway serving as the ceremonial entrance for new students during Convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: New students pass through the arch at Porter's Lodge on their first day to enter the Cistern Yard and officially sign 'the book'.
cards.source_title: Traditions - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; ceremonial walks occur during Fall Welcome Weekend.

cards.title: Attend New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Gather Under the Oaks
cards.notes: Join your classmates for the annual gathering in this iconic green space. It is the primary site for welcoming the new class and introducing academic traditions.
cards.short_summary: The historic heart of campus featuring live oaks and Randolph Hall, used for major ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation is an annual gathering in the Cistern Yard where students embark on their intellectual journeys at the College.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Celebrates New College of Charleston Students
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space accessible 24/7; events scheduled during orientation weekend.

cards.title: Join the Party on the Green
cards.subtitle: Pre-Convocation Social
cards.notes: Meet fellow new students for a social gathering behind the library before the Cougar Walk begins. It's a prime spot for making your first campus connections.
cards.short_summary: A large grassy area behind Addlestone Library used for student events and outdoor studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Party on the Green is a gathering for 500–600 students before they take the Cougar Walk to the Cistern Yard.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Celebrates New College of Charleston Students
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible campus lawn.

cards.title: Grab a First-Weekend Meal
cards.subtitle: Campus Dining Hub
cards.notes: Refuel between orientation sessions at this central dining location. It offers various food stations and is a common meeting point for freshmen.
cards.short_summary: A major campus dining facility offering diverse meal options for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Liberty St. Food Hall is listed as a primary dining location for students on campus.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Requires meal plan or payment; hours vary by semester.

cards.title: Relax by the Turtle Pond
cards.subtitle: Quiet Campus Retreat
cards.notes: Take a break in the garden outside the student center. Look for the resident turtles in the fountain while you decompress from move-in stress.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful garden area with picnic tables and a fountain located at the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stern Center Garden features picnic tables and a fountain with turtles, serving as a quiet study or break spot.
cards.source_title: Best Studies Spots On Campus At College Of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Open daily; located adjacent to the food court.

cards.title: Find Your Classrooms
cards.subtitle: Student-Led Campus Tours
cards.notes: Meet at the mall for a personalized tour to locate your Monday morning classes. Current students lead these sessions to help you navigate the historic campus.
cards.short_summary: A central campus walkway and gathering space between major academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Classroom tours with orientation interns meet at Cougar Mall to help students find their classes.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Tours typically run 11am-1pm during opening weekend.

cards.title: Explore the Historic Market
cards.subtitle: Downtown Discovery
cards.notes: Walk a few blocks off campus to browse local crafts and souvenirs. It's a classic Charleston experience for students getting to know their new city.
cards.short_summary: A historic market complex featuring local vendors, sweetgrass baskets, and regional food.
cards.evidence_claim: The Charleston City Market is a hub of activity and commerce accessible by foot from the College.
cards.source_title: The Historic Charleston City Market
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 9:30am; Night Market hours vary.

cards.title: Walk to the Pineapple Fountain
cards.subtitle: Scenic Peninsula Views
cards.notes: Take a sunset stroll to the harbor to see the famous Pineapple Fountain. It's a popular spot for students to relax and enjoy the ocean breeze.
cards.short_summary: A scenic park along the Cooper River known for its fountains and harbor views.
cards.evidence_claim: Waterfront Park is a popular attraction for students to hang out after classes with plenty of benches and grass.
cards.source_title: The Best Study Spots for CofC Students
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily; approximately 15-minute walk from campus.

cards.title: Scope Out a Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Late Night Prep
cards.notes: Visit the library to find your favorite study spot before the first week of classes. The higher floors offer quieter zones for focused work.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library featuring extensive study spaces and a Starbucks.
cards.evidence_claim: Addlestone Library offers extended hours and requires Cougar Cards for access after midnight.
cards.source_title: Hours - College of Charleston Libraries
cards.access_notes: Cougar Card required for entry after midnight; public access during day hours.

cards.title: Visit the Cougar Den
cards.subtitle: Athletic Spirit Hub
cards.notes: Check out the home of Cougar basketball. Familiarize yourself with the student section entry so you're ready for the first home game of the season.
cards.short_summary: The primary indoor sports arena for the College of Charleston athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: TD Arena has a 1,000 seat student section; entry requires a valid College of Charleston student ID.
cards.source_title: Game Day Information - TD Arena
cards.access_notes: Student section is general admission; tickets must be claimed via student portal for games.
